company_items.summary: AutoZone reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — tariff refunds provided a 145 basis point gross margin tailwind and a non-cash LIFO impact added another 105 basis points. Domestic comps came in at plus 1.6% versus the Street's plus 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year, though management noted positive comp linearity in the quarter.

MillerKnoll reported solid fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and importantly the beat holds up even excluding tariff refunds — stripping out the 11-cent tailwind, EPS was still 42 cents versus the 36-cent consensus. Guidance is mixed: fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed but EPS outlook was left unchanged.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS estimates, reporting 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, as gross margin weakness — down 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the consensus 13.85% — more than offset slightly better-than-expected revenue of $2.311 billion. Management cited a difficult macro landscape as a headwind.

Meta's Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads ahead of Zuckerberg's Connect keynote Wednesday night, and Shopify has agreed to allow Muse to complete purchases on its e-commerce platform. Amazon has blocked Muse from its platform, but investor expectations are growing increasingly bullish into the keynote catalyst.

Shopify announced it will allow Meta's Muse personal AI agent to complete purchases on its e-commerce platform, positioning Shopify as a key partner in the agentic commerce ecosystem. This is a meaningful differentiator versus Amazon, which blocked Muse access.

Quest Diagnostics shares were hit Tuesday after CMS released new Medicare payment rates for lab services that represented a larger reduction than the market had anticipated. The rate cuts are a direct headwind to revenue and margins.

Lab Corp shares sold off alongside Quest Diagnostics on the same CMS Medicare rate cut announcement, with the reduction coming in worse than expected. Both lab testing firms are under meaningful pressure on the news.

Cognex announced it will acquire RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. The deal positions Cognex deeper into the robotics and physical AI supply chain.

Viking Therapeutics reported positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in the trial. The result reinforces Viking's competitive position in the crowded but high-growth obesity drug market.

A WWD article speculated Tuesday that Capri Holdings, owner of Michael Kors and Jimmy Choo, could potentially be for sale. No official confirmation from the company, making this rumor-driven and uncertain.

tts_summary:
Here's your midday update for Tuesday, September 22nd. Markets are mixed and mostly quiet as investors sit on their hands waiting for two big catalysts — any diplomatic development on Iran at the United Nations, and a wave of artificial intelligence events kicking off tomorrow night. The S-P-500 is flat, the Nasdaq is up about 38 basis points, the Russell 2000 is up 30 basis points, but the Dow is lagging, down about 43 basis points. Treasuries are flat across the curve. Brent crude is near one hundred dollars a barrel, off modestly on hopes for a Hormuz diplomatic resolution and news that Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline may be partially coming back online after Houthi disruptions forced the Saudis back through the Strait. Gold, silver, and bitcoin are all slightly lower.

On the company side, AutoZone beat fiscal fourth quarter earnings with 56 dollars and 5 cents versus the Street's 54 dollars and 3 cents — but quality matters here. The beat was driven by tariff refunds worth 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash accounting impact worth another 105 basis points. Domestic comps missed badly, coming in at plus 1.6 percent versus the Street's plus 3.1 percent. The stock is rallying anyway on management's comment that comp linearity was positive through the quarter. MillerKnoll was a cleaner beat — 53 cents versus 36 cents, and even stripping out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind you still get 42 cents, well above consensus. THOR Industries missed — 78 cents versus 87 cents expected, gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year, and management flagged a tough macro backdrop. Viking Therapeutics reported positive results for its GLP-1 obesity drug VK2735, showing 22 percent weight loss in the trial. Meta is building momentum into tomorrow night's Connect keynote — Muse downloads are surging and Shopify has agreed to allow Muse to complete purchases on its platform, while Amazon has blocked it. Cognex is acquiring depth-sensing camera leader RealSense for roughly 500 million dollars plus additional consideration, a physical AI and robotics play. On the negative side, Quest Diagnostics and Lab Corp are both getting hit after CMS released Medicare lab service payment rates that came in worse than feared. Capri Holdings is in the news on takeover speculation from a trade publication, unconfirmed.

Sector-wise, financials are broadly under pressure — banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers all lower. Managed care is weak. Tech is bifurcated with semiconductor and AI infrastructure names outperforming while enterprise software and networking names lag. Texas Governor Abbott's move to halt data center permitting is an incremental negative for the data center build-out narrative. The next ten days are critical for artificial intelligence positioning — Meta Connect tomorrow night, OpenAI's developer day on the 29th, and Micron earnings on the 30th. How those catalysts land will likely set the tone for the sector into year-end.
